Now I'll filter only Blu-Ray entries (excluding the 'Blu-Ray' header row itself), coerce Year to numeric, sort ascending by Year, and list the earliest titles.

```python
# filename: earliest_bluray_candidates.py
import pandas as pd

fp = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/32102e3e-d12a-4209-9163-7b3a104efe5d.xlsx'
df = pd.read_excel(fp, skiprows=2)
format_markers = {'DVD', 'Blu-Ray', 'VHS', 'CD', 'Digital'}
# Propagate format
current_format = None
formats = []
for title in df['Title'].astype(str).str.strip():
    if title in format_markers:
        current_format = title
        formats.append(current_format)
    else:
        formats.append(current_format)
df['Format'] = formats

# Filter Blu-Ray items (exclude header row where Title == 'Blu-Ray')
bluray_df = df[(df['Format'] == 'Blu-Ray') & (~df['Title'].astype(str).str.strip().isin(format_markers))].copy()
bluray_df['Year'] = pd.to_numeric(bluray_df['Year'], errors='coerce')
bluray_df = bluray_df.dropna(subset=['Year'])
bluray_sorted = bluray_df.sort_values('Year', ascending=True)
print('Earliest 5 Blu-Ray rows by Year:')
print(bluray_sorted[['Title','Year']].head(5))
print('Min Year:', bluray_sorted['Year'].min())
```
